title: Lamb Biryani
subtitle: South Asian spiced lamb and basmati rice baked together
excerpt: Lamb marinated in spiced yoghurt, layered with par-cooked saffron rice, sealed, and steam-cooked together in the oven until the rice is fluffy and fragrant and the lamb is tender. The dum method: slow-cooked in its own steam.

recipe.sourceNotes: Biryani is a rice dish with roots in Persian pilaf traditions, brought to the Indian subcontinent by Mughal rulers and developed into many distinct regional varieties across South Asia. Hyderabadi biryani, Lucknow (Awadhi) biryani, Calcutta biryani, and Sindhi biryani are among the most celebrated. The defining technique is dum pukht (slow cooking in sealed steam): the marinated meat and par-cooked rice are layered in a pot, the lid is sealed with dough or foil, and the pot is cooked over a very low heat or in a low oven so the rice absorbs the meat's aromatics through steam. The lamb version is arguably the most deeply flavoured biryani, with the fat from the lamb enriching the rice during cooking.

content.text: Par-cook the rice until it is just 70% done; it will finish cooking in the dum stage. Seal the pot as tightly as possible with foil before the lid goes on; the steam must not escape. The resting period after the oven is as important as the cooking: it allows the rice to steam to completion and makes the biryani easier to serve.

content.text: Mix the lamb with the yoghurt, grated garlic, ginger, diced onion, garam masala, cumin, coriander, chilli, turmeric, and 1 tsp salt. Marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Fry the thinly sliced onions in plenty of oil over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. In the same pan, cook the marinated lamb for 10 to 15 minutes until the marinade has dried and the lamb is partially cooked and coated in the spices.

Par-cook the drained rice in heavily salted boiling water for 6 minutes; it should be 70% cooked. Drain. In a large, heavy pot with a tight-fitting lid, layer the lamb, then the rice, then the fried onions, mint, coriander, and saffron milk. Dot with butter. Cover with foil, then the lid.

Cook in the oven at 150°C / fan 130°C / gas 2 for 45 minutes. Remove from the oven and leave sealed for 10 minutes. Open the pot and gently fold the layers together once or twice with a large spoon before serving.
